entries.title: Source: the FBI is probing whether the FAA outage was caused by a software update, and doesn't believe it was due to a cyberattack or criminality (Myles Miller/Bloomberg)
The FAA announced on November 10 that it has expanded the use of SMART, an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to manage congestion, across the US (Jeremy Hsu/Ars Technica)
Sources: Moonshot AI is deactivating its Cayman holding company and moving investors' stakes to its primary operating entity in China to pave the way for an IPO (Wall Street Journal)
The FAA issues a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following "communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers" (Alex Fitzpatrick/Axios)
How Nvidia used a "scorched earth, adversarial attitude" targeting proponents of export controls in DC, invoking Trump's name to get license approvals expedited (Semafor)
Microsoft apologizes for the outage, calling it a "technical issue" from a "network capacity upgrade", and says it was "not related to cyber or AI/agents" (@microsoft)
Nvidia board says it is "in the process of selecting a search firm" for the CEO role and it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC)
Sources: Meta staffers are testing a prediction-market app called Takes, letting users wager on the outcome of questions or events using "cred", not real money (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
Dario Amodei says figuring out how much computing is needed in a year or two is Anthropic's "deepest business dilemma" due to the unpredictability of revenue (Bloomberg)
Some investors and founders say they lost an ally in Jensen Huang; Nvidia held $48B in 229 private companies as of July and offered $165B in cloud backstops (New York Times)
Claude Duet review: user-friendly, sends a helpful morning brief, and spots scheduling conflicts, but can feel like a neurotic personal assistant that nags (Allison Johnson/The Verge)
Some in China question the timing of reports on the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang; Trump is set to meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen next week (Mithil Aggarwal/NBC News)
Microsoft says Microsoft 365 availability is improving as the outage stretches into a second day, disrupting governments, hospitals, and businesses globally (Bruce Gil/Gizmodo)
Wall Street fears Jensen Huang's ouster will slow Nvidia's AI dealmaking; sources: its $500B lending consortium is in flux and at least one lender may exit (New York Times)
OpenAI disbands its standalone robotics team, moving its staff to research and Applied units, saying models like GPT-6 Astra can be directly applied to robotics (Wen Shao/Fortune)
